title: Burst sparsification and tenant cooldown — PRD concept
content:
Purpose:

This doc proposes a lightweight approach to dampen short, high-intensity bursts on Dedicated pools while preserving tenant throughput and headroom for critical traffic. The two core levers are: (1) burst sparsification — an admission-level thinning transform that reduces compute by probabilistically downsampling nonessential request tokens or lowering per-request work, and (2) tenant cooldown windows — short, configurable cool-off periods that temporarily limit aggressive reentry to burst lanes and allow the autoscaler to reestablish a stable allocation. Together these levers aim to reduce tail-load spikes, lower cost to serve bursty tenants, and reduce noisy-neighbor impact on co-tenants without resorting to hard preemption.

Why this is different / problem statement:

We already support burst credits, warm pools, and various fallback lanes. However, many customers show repeated microbursts (seconds–minutes) that cause transient SLO violations across a pool. Current mitigations either (a) preempt aggressively causing customer-visible errors, or (b) rely on large warm headroom which is expensive. Burst sparsification + cooldown is a softer, model-preserving approach: make each burst request slightly cheaper or less frequent in a way that is minimally noticeable for best-effort workloads and preserves full fidelity for pinned SLO-critical traffic.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce p99 latency violations during short bursts by 30–60% (measured across affected Dedicated pools).
- Reduce extra warmhead/idle capacity required to sustain typical microburst profiles by 20% in simulated workloads.
- Keep user-visible quality regressions within acceptable thresholds for best-effort classes: >95% of responses unchanged; for changed responses, measured quality delta small by eval hooks.
- Provide clear telemetry (burst_sparsity_rate, tenant_cooldown_seconds, compute_reclaimed_ms) and operator runbook.

Non-goals:
- Replace existing preemption or hard-eviction controls.
- Make permanent fidelity changes to pinned SLO endpoints.

User personas / use cases:
- Startup A uses Dedicated for nightly batch plus sporadic API spikes that happen when customers run heavy exports. Allowing a small fraction of tokens to be thinned during spikes keeps the API responsive for interactive customers on the same pool.
- Enterprise B schedules model evaluation jobs that produce short transient spikes; cooldown prevents repeated immediate resubmission loops that exhaust warm pools.
- Platform team wants a conservative, observable knob they can enable per-tenant to trade minor quality variance for reduced tail latency and cost during bursts.

Design overview (high-level):

1) Admission-level sparsification transform
- Where: Admission proxy (ingress) before requests reach the router/batcher.
- What it does: For a request flagged as eligible (by tenant policy or dynamic signal), run a lightweight decision to apply one of: token sampling (drop up to N non-essential tokens from long generation prompts), prefix trimming, or early-stop heuristics for streaming requests. The transform is deterministic-probabilistic (seeded by request id) and annotated in the request metadata so downstream is aware of the transform.
- Granularity: per-request. Policies may declare a target sparsity fraction (e.g., 0.05–0.30) and a mode (token-trim, prefix-elide, quantized-path).
- Fallback: If applied but downstream detects a quality regression (via lightweight eval hooks or length mismatch), it can mark the request for re-run on a fidelity lane (counts against retry budget).

2) Tenant cooldown windows
- Where: Tenancy controller / quota manager layer that tracks burst events per-tenant and per-organization.
- What it does: When a tenant crosses a configurable burst threshold (burst credits consumed or short-term concurrency > X), attach a cooldown timer to that tenant id for a short period (e.g., 30–300s). While in cooldown: new requests are subject to higher probability of sparsification or are routed to slow-fallback lanes with lower concurrency. Cooldowns use a decay schedule (exponential backoff) so repeated burst events progressively lengthen the cooldown within a bounded cap.
- Overrides: Admins can whitelist endpoints to be cooldown-exempt (pinned SLOs).

3) Policy / config model
- Tenant-level policy fields (examples):
  - sparsification_enabled: true|false
  - sparsity_mode: token_trim | prefix_elide | reduce_steps | quantized_fastpath
  - target_sparsity: string percentage e.g. "0.10"
  - cooldown_base_secs: "60"
  - cooldown_max_secs: "900"
  - burst_threshold_concurrency: "20"
  - burst_threshold_tokens_per_30s: "50000"
- System-level defaults applied to pools with an opt-in per-tenant override.

4) Observability and evaluation hooks
- Instrumentation: emit per-request tags: sparsified:true/false, sparsity_fraction, cooldown_active:true/false, re-run_flag:true/false. Aggregate metrics by tenant and pool: p95/p99 latency, compute-ms saved, sparsified_request_ratio.
- Quality eval: lightweight sampling pipeline that replays sparsified requests in a parallel fidelity lane (on a small sample) and calculates simple deltas (token overlap, perplexity delta, application-specific metric). Alert on regressions.

5) Autoscaler interaction and capacity accounting
- Treat reclaimed compute from sparsification as temporary headroom; we surface it in the autoscaler telemetry but do not change committed capacity until sustained savings observed for a configurable window (e.g., 15m).
- Cooldown reduces effective concurrency signal from tenants which the autoscaler uses to avoid overreacting to microbursts.

API and Console UX
- New tenant policy page entries in Console -> Dedicated -> Tenants: toggle for "Burst sparsification (experimental)", sliders for target sparsity and cooldown base.
- Exportable metrics and a per-tenant burst timeline view showing active cooldown windows and reclaimed compute.

Operational details / runbook
- Enabling: start in monitoring-only mode (sparsified flag set but no transform applied). Collect evaluation samples for 48–72 hours.
- Pilot: pick 5 non-critical tenants with known microburst profiles and enable conservative sparsity (0.05–0.10) + cooldown_base_secs=60. Monitor quality evals and p99 latency for pool.
- Rollback: if sampled quality regressions exceed threshold (e.g., >5% of samples exceed critical delta) or if operator-visible errors increase, toggle off per-tenant policy.
- Incident response: if a pool-wide SLO degrades unexpectedly after enabling, disable system-level sparsification immediately and investigate correlating cooldown events.

Success metrics / instrumentation for rollout evaluation
- Technical: p99 latency reduction during identified microburst windows; compute-ms reclaimed; autoscaler oscillation frequency.
- Business: customer-reported incidents; any customer complaints about quality; net cost delta for Dedicated pools.

Security and compliance considerations
- No user data leaves the serving path. Sparsification is an inline transform; logged metadata avoids storing redacted content.
- For regulated tenants, ensure sparsification is opt-out and clearly documented in contract/TOU.

Risks and mitigations
- Quality regressions: mitigate with small default sparsity, opt-in pilots, and evaluation replay.
- Retry storms: re-runs of sparsified requests could create loops; cap re-run budget and surface re-run counts to ops.
- Complexity in autoscaler signals: mark reclaimed compute as provisional and require sustained signal before capacity changes.

Unresolved questions / open items
- Exact sparsification heuristics for different model families (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder). Need applied-ML experiments.
- Sampling rate necessary for reliable eval signals without incurring high extra compute.
- Biz policy: when should chargeback reflect sparsified execution? Do we bill full or reduced units for sparsified requests?

Next steps / roadmap (proposed):
- Nov–Dec 2025: Prototype sparsifier in ingress for token_trim+prefix_elide; enable monitoring-only mode.
- Jan 2026: Pilot with 5 tenants on a single region pool; run quality evals and tune policies.
- Feb–Mar 2026: Add cooldown scheduler with decay/backoff; surface console controls and per-tenant toggles.
- Apr 2026+: Broader rollout, autoscaler integration for sustained reclaimed compute, and policy billing discussion.

Appendix A: example policy (JSON-like, for operator copy)
- sparsification_enabled: true
- sparsity_mode: token_trim
- target_sparsity: "0.08"
- cooldown_base_secs: "120"
- cooldown_max_secs: "600"
- burst_threshold_concurrency: "25"

Appendix B: quick experiment plan for applied-ML
1) Take corpus of 5k representative requests from bursty tenants.
2) Apply token_trim at 5%,10%,20% and measure delta for task-specific metrics.
3) Run human spot-check for semantic drift on sample of 200 per condition.
4) Feed results into threshold table for console defaults.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative and designed as an additive, opt-in set of controls rather than an automatic aggressive throttle. Feedback particularly requested on: default target_sparsity, cooldown decay function, and acceptable sample sizes for quality telemetry.
